approach: List the four forces, then split each one first into horizontal and vertical parts, then into parts along and across the incline.

steps.text: Four forces act on the body: normal reaction N perpendicular to the incline, weight w straight down, string tension T at 30° to the incline surface, and friction f along the incline.
N is perpendicular to a 30° incline, so it is tilted 30° from the vertical. Resolve it horizontally and vertically.
steps.equation: N_horizontal = N sin 30° = 0.5N, N_vertical = N cos 30° = 0.87N

steps.text: Weight acts straight down, so it has no horizontal part.
The string is at 30° to the incline, and the incline is at 30° to the horizontal, so the string is at 60° to the horizontal.
steps.equation: T_horizontal = T cos 60° = 0.5T, T_vertical = T sin 60° = 0.87T

steps.text: Friction acts along the incline surface, tilted 30° from the horizontal, same as the incline itself.
steps.equation: f_horizontal = f cos 30° = 0.87f, f_vertical = f sin 30° = 0.5f

steps.text: Now resolve parallel and perpendicular to the plane. N is entirely perpendicular, and f is entirely parallel, by definition.
steps.equation: N_parallel = 0, N_perp = N; f_parallel = f, f_perp = 0

steps.text: Weight makes 30° with the perpendicular to the plane; tension makes 30° with the plane itself.
steps.equation: w_parallel = w sin 30° = 0.5w, w_perp = w cos 30° = 0.87w; T_parallel = T cos 30° = 0.87T, T_perp = T sin 30° = 0.5T

final_answer.value: (a) horizontal, vertical: N (0.5N, 0.87N); w (0, w); T (0.5T, 0.87T); f (0.87f, 0.5f). (b) parallel, perpendicular to plane: N (0, N); w (0.5w, 0.87w); T (0.87T, 0.5T); f (f, 0)

common_mistakes.text: Resolving the string tension at 30° to the horizontal instead of 30° to the incline, which actually puts it at 60° to the horizontal.
Swapping sine and cosine when resolving the normal reaction, giving N_horizontal = 0.87N and N_vertical = 0.5N.
